prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a high-fidelity desktop APPLICATION INTERFACE design mockup for a new "Prepare a delivery" feature inside Drag Shelf. This is proposed software, not a marketing poster or photograph. Output a crisp flat front-facing screenshot-like UI, landscape approximately 1440x1000, no perspective or physical monitor mockup, with readable professionally typeset text. Reference image 1 is the actual current Drag Shelf interface and is the visual identity authority: inherit warm charcoal #242520, secondary #2c2d27, cream #f4f5ee text, muted olive secondary text, yellow #f5c63a primary actions, softly rounded containers and simple consistent stroke icons. Reference 2 is the app icon; use it small in the app header. Keep original visual identity; expand the usable desktop workspace. No gradients, neon, glass decoration, fake charts, ratings, customer claims or AI branding. The user's job is prepare files for a client, understand the checks and proposed output, and preserve originals. Use one labeled "Sample project" named "Brand handoff". Show source filenames such as Brand-guide.pdf, Logo-final.png, Logo-final-copy.png, and Source-files.zip. A "Client delivery" recipe checks Final assets, Source files, Invoice and Instructions. Invoice is missing; mark it "Not added" and provide an action, do not imply all checks passed. Duplicate image copies are detected. Preparation supports consistent filenames, resize images to 1920 px, a README, and export to a new folder or ZIP. Clearly say "Originals stay unchanged". Show a practical output preview with a folder tree and original → output filename examples. Distinguish optional checks from blocking missing-file errors. Clear primary button "Review preparation", secondary "Save recipe"; compact language selector "English". Mockup text is English; ensure space for a Khmer variant during implementation. Precisely align controls, generous but purposeful spacing, usable target sizes, no repeated nested cards. All visible content must look like functional application controls and realistic sample data. Include the option label small in the image header, not as a poster heading. Option A — Delivery workspace. Composition: one unified app window with small logo/header at top, large title "Prepare a delivery" and subtitle "Brand handoff" beneath. A quiet horizontal progress line "Collect / Check / Prepare / Export" across the upper edge, with Check highlighted. Main content uses TWO generous columns with roughly 55/45 split: left column source-file list followed by a compact readiness checklist with 2 specific findings; right column preparation controls above a live output folder preview. Use clear list rows and restrained dividers rather than a card grid. At bottom a single continuous action bar has "Originals stay unchanged" left, "Save recipe" quiet action, and yellow "Review preparation" right. The dominant focal moment is the output folder preview beside the readiness findings. This should feel like a calm workbench where the full job can be seen at once.
